messages:
Sam: Quick follow-up from the kernel selection RFC — we need to pick a dequant strategy for attention ops (FP8/INT8/INT4). Two options on the table: a) fused-dequant kernels that accept quantized inputs and emit float outputs inside the kernel, or b) keep kernels pure and do 'lazy' dequant in a separate pass before op invocation. Thoughts?

Priya: +1 on fused-dequant for the hot path. avoids memcpy and extra tensors. latency win for 1-token tails. but more kernel surface area to maintain. :thinking_face:

Maya: Fused looks great perf-wise but I'm worried about QA/regressions for generation quality. mixing dequant inside attention means we have to revalidate every attention variant (k/v cache, rotary, 2D attn, etc). heavy test matrix.

Leo: Infra perspective: fused reduces device-host mem churn but complicates kernel packaging and versioning. if we ship multiple fused kernels per quant format + seq-len profile, bumping a kernel becomes a breaking change for model variants.

Sam: Good points. I sketched a middle-ground: keep canonical small "dequant shim" that runs on the same device and sits between model ORT graph and kernels, but allow an optimized fused path we enable via runtime feature flag for specific models. Runtime would route by policy: prefer fused when model+batch fits resource profile; otherwise use shim.

Priya: That feels pragmatic. We can implement a minimal device shim kernel that just views quant buffer + scale params and materializes a transient float view in-place (no copies) using a custom allocator and then call existing attention kernel. This keeps the kernel interface stable.

Maya: Can you paste the pseudo-config for routing? want to make sure evals can opt-in/opt-out.

Sam: Sure — rough runtime config: 

```json
{"quant_dequant_strategy": "auto",
 "fused_profiles": ["llama-13b:shortseq", "rhino-7b:all-seq"],
 "fallback_to_shim": true,
 "metrics_tag": "dequant-route"
}
```

Priya: Nice. We should add a safety gate to disable fused for any model with failing unit prompt sets (quality regression detected). Redwood Optimize can push a signal.

Maya: Agree. Also need a test harness story: nightly matrix that runs fused vs shim across a small curated suite (<100 prompts) with per-token log-prob diffs. If diffs exceed threshold -> auto-disable.

Leo: Ops note: turning on fused for Dedicated customers needs ability to pin to kernel artifact version and rollback. also handshake with rollout system so can canary deploy one customer or route 5% traffic.

Sam: Implementation tasks I see: 1) define stable attention kernel ABI (quant buffers + scale metadata format), 2) implement device shim kernel (in-place mapping), 3) build fused kernel prototypes for FP8/INT8/INT4 attention, 4) runtime routing + feature flag, 5) eval harness + auto-disable signal.

Priya: For ABI, propose a tiny header struct passed as tensor meta: `quant_format`, `scales_ptr`, `scale_count`, `zero_point` (if int8). keep it backward compatible so existing kernels ignore unknown header.

Maya: That will help. Also log per-request route decision into console/tracing so SRE/QA can filter by route. we need token-level latency and delta-quality metrics emitted.

Leo: +1. add quota/cost bucket attribution too so customers see cost benefits.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled: fused-dequant-proto -> staging at 2026-03-21T02:10Z.

Sam: OK next steps: Priya + Maya pair on shim + harness. Leo to write rollout doc/rollback knobs. I'll spike fused kernels for int4 and fp8 and push perf numbers next week. Raising action items on the RFC thread. Thanks all. :rocket:
